title: Operational Risk, Rogue Trading Disasters, Barings Bank, LTCM, and Risk Management Lessons
prerequisites: Futures and options margin mechanics and mark-to-market procedures
Value at Risk (VaR) and stress testing risk metrics
Corporate governance and internal control principles
learningOutcomes: Define operational risk in derivatives and explain why abnormal trading outperformance often signals hidden tail risk ([fact-01], [fact-03]).
Enforce mandatory independent daily mark-to-market accounting and the segregation of trading and settlement duties ([fact-02]).
Analyze historical rogue trading disasters (Barings Bank, Société Générale, Allfirst) and institutional fund collapses (LTCM) ([fact-04], [fact-05], [fact-06], [fact-07], [fact-08]).
Distinguish gross terminal payoff from net economic profit and mandate rigorous stress testing alongside VaR models ([fact-09], [fact-10]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: In derivatives markets, abnormal outperformance almost always reflects the unacknowledged accumulation of catastrophic short option tail risk or hidden leverage rather than mystical foresight ([fact-03]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Front-office traders must never value their own positions or maintain discretionary off-ledger reserve accounts; independent middle-office and back-office staff must execute daily mark-to-market accounting ([fact-02]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: VaR models fail completely during extreme tail events; institutions must enforce rigorous stress testing modeling asset illiquidity and margin call spikes during historic crises ([fact-10]).

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: Nick Leeson held over 27,000 long Nikkei 225 futures contracts representing over $7,000,000,000 in nominal exposure alongside unhedged short straddles. When the Kobe earthquake struck and the Nikkei plummeted 15%, cumulative margin calls wiped out Barings' entire equity base.
activeRecallQuiz.question: 1) What primary organizational control failure enabled Nick Leeson to hide £827 million in losses at Barings Bank? 2) Why do normal VaR models fail during systemic market crises?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: Correctly identifying the downside risk and margin constraints.
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Detailed pedagogical explanation grounded in source principles.

coreTakeaways: Operational risk arises from failed internal processes and weak controls, making the strict segregation of front-office and back-office duties non-negotiable ([fact-01], [fact-02]).

Historical derivative disasters like Barings, Société Générale, and LTCM stem from rogue trading, hidden leverage, and unhedged tail risks rather than bad market luck ([fact-04], [fact-06], [fact-08]).
Daily independent mark-to-market accounting and rigorous stress testing are mandatory to capture low-probability catastrophic tail events that bypass standard VaR models ([fact-02], [fact-10]).
